entries.summary: Describes the two Halakhic forms of excommunication, cherem (civic ostracism) and the more serious karet (spiritual death), including that karet victims are treated as excommunicates and how either can be lifted.
quotes: Characters punished through karet are treated as excommunicates as described in Chapter Four.
The Talmud identifies 24 crimes that may be punished by cherem.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine, Chapter Four (excommunication)

entries.title: Jewish Proscriptions Against Magic
entries.summary: Lists the mitzvot that forbid Jews from many kinds of magic and notes how this conflicts with being a Gifted Hermetic magus, with Karaite practice offering an accommodation.
quotes: It is difficult for a Gifted Jew to remain true to both his faith and his magical arts.

entries.title: The City of Luz (Celestial Regio)
entries.summary: A Divine regio where those inside do not die; it explains how to summon a pathway to it, how recovery rolls and aging behave inside, and the penalty for leaving after a long stay.
quotes: It takes a Purity (or Merkavah) + Intervention miraculous effect of base 35 to summon a pathway to the city gates
any rolls of 0 or less impose an Aging Point in any physical Characteristic

entries.title: Virtues Forbidden to Jewish Characters
entries.summary: Explains which Social Status and other Virtues Jewish characters cannot take, and that they must take Educated (Hebrew) to gain Academic Abilities.
quotes: Both Knight and Landed Noble imply a feudal position within society, which Jews cannot occupy.
must take Educated (Hebrew) instead to gain access to Academic Abilities

entries.title: Outsider Flaw for Jewish Characters
entries.summary: Non-magus Jewish characters typically take a form of the Outsider Flaw (Major for companions, new Minor for grogs), which is incompatible with the Hermetic Magus Social Status Virtue.
quotes: Non-magi Jewish characters typically take a form of the Outsider Flaw

entries.title: Jewish Grogs Must Take Outsider
entries.summary: Jewish grogs must take the Minor Outsider Flaw and live in a Jewish community or covenant, since a Jew outside such places is too conspicuous to be a background character.
quotes: Jewish grogs must take the Outsider Minor Flaw

entries.title: Jewish Companions Must Take Outsider
entries.summary: Jewish companions must take the Major Outsider Flaw to represent the prejudice they face outside Jewish communities and the covenant.
quotes: Jewish companions must take the Outsider Major Flaw

groups.title: The Infernal Realm
groups.intro: The Infernal, sin, temptation and corruption.

entries.title: Infernal Creatures
entries.summary: Infernal creatures may take attractive forms, and their lies cannot be detected by Magic realm powers, though ordinary investigation can still reveal the truth.
quotes: The lies of creatures that belong to the Infernal realm cannot be detected by the powers of the Magic realm.

entries.title: Infernal Auras
entries.summary: Describes the effects of Infernal auras on travelers and magic, that magic can detect them, and that they wax at night and wane on holy days.
quotes: Of greater concern to magi, Infernal auras interfere with the use of magic.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal, pp.10-17

entries.title: Sources of Infernal Auras
entries.summary: Infernal auras arise from serious or repeated sin and from infernal creatures or powers, with examples of the strengths produced.
quotes: In an area with no aura, a cruel and premeditated murder can create a level 1 aura.

entries.title: Heresy and Corruption
entries.summary: Guidance for storyguides on when heresy actually counts as Infernal rather than merely mistaken: most heretics are sincere believers, and a false teaching is Infernal only when it leads to real sinful acts.
quotes: A wrong teaching only becomes Infernal when it leads people directly to sinful behavior, and hence to damnation.

entries.title: The Feast of All Souls and the Dominion
entries.summary: Origin of the Feast of All Souls on 2 November, with its aura effect: on that day the Dominion is weaker than usual, Infernal auras are stronger, and some of the dead walk again.
quotes: Infernal auras increase in strength by one, and some of the dead walk once more.

entries.title: Mortuary Masses
entries.summary: Describes the Infernal perversion of a funeral Mass said for a living person, which is held to cause death and is treated as murder.
quotes: It is widely believed that if a funeral Mass is celebrated for a man or woman still living, he will die.

entries.title: Cluniac Influence on Petitioning the Church
entries.requires: Favor of a Cluniac prior or abbot
entries.summary: Cluniac abbots and priors carry extra weight with the Church hierarchy, giving a bonus to Petitioning the Church totals when their favor is won.
quotes: Gaining the favor of a Cluniac prior or abbot gives a +1 bonus to totals for Petitioning the Church (see Chapter 3: The Diocese) over and above the usual bonuses.

related.text: Chapter 3: The Diocese, Petitioning the Church

entries.title: The Corrupt Cluniacs
entries.requires: Saga option: the Cluniacs are Infernally corrupt
entries.summary: How to run the Cluniac order as the corrupt order in a saga: its history of corruption, the Goetic Favored Abilities and Supernatural Ability Corruption of its monks, profaned rites that create Infernal vis, Debauched Auras, and bound ghosts.
quotes: The corrupt Cluniacs have Favored Abilities of the Goetic Arts of Ablating, Binding, Commanding, and Summoning.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal pp.14, 91, 96, 114-120

entries.title: Cistercian Influence on Petitioning the Church
entries.summary: The Cistercians' standing with the papacy gives a bonus to Petitioning the Church totals when a Cistercian abbot's favor is gained.
quotes: gaining the favor of a Cistercian abbot gives a +3 bonus to totals for Petitioning the Church (See Chapter 3: The Diocese) over and above the usual bonuses.

related.text: Chapter 3: The Diocese, Petitioning the Church

entries.title: The Corrupt Cistercians (Joachimite Illuminati)
entries.requires: Saga option: the Cistercians are Infernally corrupt
entries.summary: How to run the Cistercian order as the corrupt order: the Joachimite heresy and the secret Illuminati society inside the order, with its three informal degrees of initiation culminating in an inner circle that teaches Maleficia through an Unholy Tradition.
quotes: There are three degrees of initiation into the group, though these are not formal ranks as in a mystery cult.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal p.133
Realms of Power: The Infernal p.128

entries.title: Vallumbrosan Papal Influence
entries.requires: Support of a Vallumbrosan abbot; petition addressed to the papacy or curia
entries.summary: Vallumbrosan influence over the papacy adds a large bonus to the total of a petition made to the pope or curia, on top of the normal bonus for an abbot's support.
quotes: If the papacy or curia are the recipients of a petition, add +5 to the total in addition to the normal bonus for the support of an abbot.

related.text: Chapter 3: The Diocese, Petitioning the Church

entries.title: If the Vallumbrosans are Corrupt
entries.requires: Saga option: the Vallumbrosans are Infernally corrupt
entries.summary: How to run the Vallumbrosans as a diabolist order: monks are worn down until they can be offered a pact, bargaining for Virtues or loss of Flaws, with a limited term to recruit a successor before the soul is claimed.
quotes: If they leave, they have seven years to find someone else to sign the pact, or they die, their soul claimed by hell.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal p.94

entries.title: Infernal Vis
entries.summary: Introduces Infernally tainted vis, which looks ordinary to Hermetic detection but endangers non-Infernal users, and the temporary Personality Trait imposed by prolonged contact with it.
quotes: The imposed trait either starts at a score of +1, or increases the trait by 1 if the magus already possesses it.

related.text: Chapter 4: The Infernal Legions, Common Powers

entries.title: Vis Infesta
entries.summary: The mildest Infernal vis: it adds no extra botch dice beyond raw vis but makes any botch more severe, and experimentation in enchantments always yields the worst result.
quotes: one extra botch die per pawn of vis

entries.title: Vis Sordida
entries.summary: Potent but dangerous Infernal vis that boosts casting totals and Source Quality at the cost of extra botch dice, and corrupts levels of effects in items prepared with it. Includes a worked enchanting example.
quotes: Each pawn of vis sordida used to enhance a casting total adds five to the roll, rather than the +2 of standard vis.
Using vis sordida always incurs three extra botch dice per pawn used
ten levels of effects in the item are corrupted for every pawn of vis sordida used

entries.title: Vis Prava
entries.summary: The vilest Infernal vis: any roll using it is automatically a zero with extra botch dice, studying from it causes Warping, and enchanting with it ruins the item; it is far better for Infernally aligned wizards.
quotes: rolling two extra botch dice for every pawn of vis prava used
vis prava offers a +5 bonus to Casting Totals per pawn employed

entries.title: What Counts as Sin
entries.summary: Explains how the storyguide judges whether an act is sinful: aiding the Infernal always is, while other acts depend on whether they are selfish or secret.

entries.title: Types of Sin
entries.summary: Distinguishes mortal sins from venial sins and notes that compelled or inadvertent acts are not sins, but dealing with the Infernal always stains the soul.

entries.title: Sinful Traits
entries.summary: Optional method of tying each Personality Trait to a virtue or vice, with a table of the seven deadly sins and their related traits, so that sin-related rolls can be called for by category.
quotes: When dealing with opposing traits, treat the trait's value as negative.

entries.title: Redemption
entries.summary: Notes that any sinner, however corrupt, may escape Hell by truly repenting, with the means of absolution depending on faith.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine, Chapters 4, 5, 6

entries.title: Gaining Confidence through Sin
entries.summary: Characters with a sinful Personality Trait can earn Confidence Points by indulging in that sin for a season or through a ritualised act that also costs a Warping Point; even characters without Confidence can bank and spend the points.
quotes: Either activity yields a Confidence Point upon completion.
Generally speaking, venial sins are sufficient for traits of +3 or less

entries.title: Infernal Influence
entries.summary: Infernalists inspire temporary sinful Personality Traits in willing followers through a season of personal influence or a short ceremony, with the strength set by a Presence + Leadership roll.
quotes: simple die + Presence + Leadership
Infernal Influence: simple die + Presence + Leadership
traits gained from personal influence can linger as long as a year, while those from ceremonial influence usually fade within about a week

entries.title: Tarnish
entries.summary: Infernalists tarnish an Infernal aura by giving it a sinful Personality Trait, using a stress roll on Presence + Leadership; the tarnish fades over time.
quotes: Tarnishing an aura: stress die + Presence + Leadership
its value decreases by one each morning

entries.title: False Powers
entries.summary: Explains Powers aligned with the Magic or Faerie realms that are subtly tainted by the Infernal, how Divine investigation perceives them, and how Powers become False through Warping, botches or infernal interference.
quotes: False Powers are no different from any other Supernatural Virtues or Flaws, save that Divine Powers (and some Infernal ones) perceive them as unholy

entries.title: Realm Affiliations (Infernal Virtues and Abilities)
entries.summary: A table of the Supernatural Virtues, Flaws and Abilities in this book with the realm each is affiliated to for realm interaction, and notes on aura penalties and re-flavouring Powers for other realms.
quotes: | Ablating | Infernal | Chapter 11 |

entries.title: True Name of (Being)
entries.summary: Explains that a True Name is learned through Realm Lore study and lets the character affect a being as if with a permanent Arcane Connection.
quotes: the character can affect it as if she had a permanent Arcane Connection to it

entries.title: Profaning the Holy
entries.summary: Rules for turning a holy object or relic into a pawn of Infernal vis by spending Confidence or overcoming Faith, with example uses such as the Host.
quotes: To profane a holy object costs the character a point of Confidence.
the character profaning it must have a Confidence Score greater than the relic's Faith Score to succeed

entries.title: Becoming Infernal
entries.summary: Explains how a being with another realm's Might can become Infernal, with its Might converting to Infernal Might, and why the reverse is rare.
quotes: when a character with Divine, Faerie, or Magic Might becomes an infernalist, her Might Score becomes Infernal Might instead

entries.title: Infernal Hierarchy and Reputation
entries.summary: Introduces Infernal Reputations, the starting Infernal Reputation of level 1 and the Hierarchy Score used in Infernal Power formulas.
quotes: This is simply the same as the score of the highest Reputation possessed by the character.
may begin with an appropriate Infernal Reputation of level 1

entries.title: Vituperation
entries.summary: The backlash an infernalist faces after gaining Warping Points or losing control of Infernal power: a resistance roll, a possible spell in Hell lasting by Warping Score, an Aging roll including Warping Score, and possible Confidence gains.
quotes: Warping Score + Number of Warping Points gained + Hierarchy Score + local aura + stress die (no botch)
Aging Roll: stress die (no botch) + (age / 10, rounded up) – living conditions modifier + Warping Score

entries.title: Infernal Sacrifice
entries.summary: Ritual sacrifices add a bonus to an infernalist's effect total depending on the victim, at the cost of about an hour of ritual.
quotes: | animal, black | +6 |
| human, innocent | +10 |

groups.title: Sacraments and rites
groups.intro: The sacraments and religious rites and their effects.

entries.title: Possession and Exorcism
entries.summary: An exorcist spends a Confidence or Faith Point and generates an Exorcism Total, which succeeds if it meets an Ease Factor equal to the Might Points the demon has invested in the possessed victim; ordination as exorcist, holy water and a crucifix add bonuses.
quotes: Exorcism Total: Stress Die + Bonuses
If the Exorcism Total equals or exceeds an Ease Factor equal to the number of Might Points invested in the energumen by the demon, then the demon is exorcised.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal p.32 Possession

entries.title: The Sacraments
entries.summary: Treats the seven Sacraments as supernatural Divine powers that need no Penetration but require willing participants, with a Faith Point available from each and specific effects for baptism, confirmation, Mass, marriage, penance, ordination and extreme unction.
quotes: A character may not have more than 1 Faith Point from each Sacrament.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.74 Sacraments

entries.title: Exorcism (Christian rite)
entries.summary: Describes how the Christian exorcism rite works mechanically: it either lets the possessed roll to shake off a resistible power or is a prayer for a miracle, costs a Confidence or Faith point, and gains bonuses from holy items and extra Faith points.
quotes: The rite costs the exorcist a Confidence (or Faith) point to perform properly.
each gives a +1 to the possessed character's total

entries.title: Invoking Muslim Holy Forbears (Baraka)
entries.requires: Muslim character in a Dominion setting
entries.summary: Muslims seek baraka from venerated figures by reusing the Christian saint-invocation mechanics, with changes: they must be at the figure's shrine, may always invoke the Qur'an, and never threaten forbears.
quotes: Muslim characters may attempt to invoke baraka from holy forbears using the same mechanics as those given above for invoking Christian saints
Muslims may always invoke the power of the Qur'an, no matter where they are.
Muslims never threaten their holy forbears.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine, Mythic Christianity, Saints

entries.title: Muslim Invocation Modifiers Table
entries.summary: Table of situational modifiers applied to a Muslim's attempt to invoke baraka from a holy forbear, covering Personality Trait, aura, feast days, relics, donations, peril and sins.
quotes: Highest Muslim Personality Trait | + value of the Trait
No zakat paid within a year | –3

entries.title: Khawass al-Qur'an (Invoking the Qur'an)
entries.summary: The Qur'an itself acts as a holy figure that can be invoked anywhere, using the same method as a forbear, to gain earthly benefits from recitation.
quotes: In game terms, the Qur'an itself may be invoked in the same way as a forbear, in an attempt to gain earthly benefits.

entries.title: Shahada: Effect on Infernal Creatures
entries.summary: Speaking the Muslim testimony of faith aloud causes brief discomfort to Infernal creatures that hear it, and pain to a rare few that are especially vulnerable.
quotes: Any creature belonging to the Infernal realm who hears someone say the shahada out loud suffers momentary discomfort.

entries.title: Salat: Ritual Prayer Raises Dominion Aura
entries.requires: Muslim ritual prayer in an Islamic Dominion aura
entries.summary: Ritual prayer five times daily temporarily strengthens an Islamic Dominion aura while it is taking place.
quotes: Any Islamic Dominion aura in which ritual prayer (salat, not du'a') is taking place has its score raised by one for the duration of the prayer.

entries.title: Zakat: Alms-Tax and the Infernal
entries.summary: Infernal creatures cannot handle goods or money given as zakat without suffering great pain, until another person has touched them.
quotes: Creatures belonging to the Infernal realm may not handle money or goods if they are being physically given to them as payment of the zakat, and they suffer excruciating pain if they attempt to do so.

entries.title: Sawm: Ramadan Fast Raises Dominion Aura
entries.summary: Muslim Dominion auras are strengthened throughout the month of Ramadan, when Muslims fast.
quotes: The score of Muslim Dominion Auras increases by one during the month of Ramadan.

entries.title: The Muslim Calendar and Holiday Auras
entries.requires: Muslim Dominion aura during a Muslim holiday
entries.summary: Lists the months and holidays of the Muslim lunar calendar and gives the aura bonus for holidays, which stacks with the bonus from ritual prayer.
quotes: The scores of Muslim Dominion auras are increased by one during Muslim holidays.

entries.title: Hajj: Pilgrimage Rewards
entries.requires: Muslim character who completes the hajj
entries.summary: A Muslim completing the pilgrimage to Mecca gains a Pious Personality Trait and Faith Points, which can be regained by repeating the hajj but never raised above a cap.
quotes: A Muslim who has completed the hajj gains a Personality Trait of Pious +3
The Muslim also gains 3 Faith Points.

entries.title: Mosque Dominion Auras
entries.summary: Gives typical Dominion aura strengths for ordinary and famous mosques and notes that prayer or the Ramadan fast raises them further.
quotes: Most mosques have a Dominion aura of 4, while major, famous mosques will usually have auras of 5

entries.title: Mecca and Medina Auras
entries.summary: Dominion auras in Mecca and Medina are stronger than normal, with specific scores for the haram and the Mosque of the Prophet.
quotes: Here the Dominion aura has a score of 10
This holy site has a Dominion aura of 9.

entries.title: Aqsa Mosque and Dome of the Rock Auras
entries.summary: Gives the mixed Dominion auras on Jerusalem's Temple Mount and notes Muslims may pray at the Dome of the Rock for a blessing of Muhammad.
quotes: The Dome of the Rock has a Dominion aura of 10

entries.title: Muslim Birth Rituals and True Names
entries.summary: Muslim birth rituals protect a child's name from being used as a True Name in supernatural activities, just as Christian baptism does.
quotes: The rituals associated with the birth have the effect of rendering the child's name unusable as a True Name in supernatural activities

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine, baptism and True Names

entries.title: Muslim Funerals and Summoning Ghosts
entries.summary: Properly buried Muslims wait in their graves until the Last Judgment, so only Muslim ghosts lacking a funeral can be magically summoned, and prophets and martyrs cannot be summoned at all.
quotes: This means that only Muslim ghosts that have not been given a Muslim funeral may be summoned to the world of the living by magic.

groups.title: Divine and Infernal Warping
groups.intro: Warping from the Divine and the Infernal.

entries.title: Divine Warping (overview)
entries.summary: Introduces Divine Warping, the Dominion-flavoured form of Warping, and the Divine Ascent peculiar to holy mystics.

entries.title: Causes of Divine Warping
entries.summary: Divine Warping comes from Divine auras, powerful Divine effects and Divine botches; it uses normal Warping mechanics with different flavour, and those with Faith Points or holy powers avoid aura Warping.
quotes: There is no mechanical difference between types of Warping.

entries.title: Divine Auras and Warping
entries.summary: Strong Divine auras in large churches are a common source of Divine Warping, though many residents are protected by Faith Points or abilities.

entries.title: Miracles and Warping
entries.summary: Witnessing a sufficiently high-level miracle gives a Warping Point, except for those it was meant to benefit.
quotes: A character in the presence of a miracle whose level is thirty or greater gains one Warping Point.

entries.title: Divine and Holy Powers and Warping
entries.summary: Powers of Divine beings and holy powers also cause Warping once their level is high enough.
quotes: will also cause Warping if the level of the power is thirty or higher

entries.title: Divine Warping from Botches
entries.summary: Using a holy power or divine supernatural ability gives Warping Points based on zeros rolled on a botch die.
quotes: One Warping Point is gained for each zero on a botch die when using a holy power or divine supernatural ability.

entries.title: The Divine Ascent (overview)
entries.summary: Holy mystics undergo a unique form of Warping, the Divine Ascent, in one of three forms (Gloom, Form, Unity) that replace the normal Effects of Warping; there is no final Ascent, and characters with only True Faith get generic Warping.
quotes: which replace the normal "Effects of Warping" rules

entries.title: Divine Ascension roll
entries.summary: When a holy character gains two or more Warping Points from one event they roll to resist being lifted into the Divine; failure triggers a form of the Ascent and extra Warping Points equal to the margin of failure.
quotes: DIVINE ASCENSION: Presence + Concentration (or Meditation) + stress die vs. Warping Score + Number of Warping Points Gained + True Faith Score + local aura + stress die (no botch)

entries.title: Experiencing the Ascent (duration)
entries.summary: Describes the visionary experience of the Ascent, how long it lasts (in days, later months), True Faith shortening it, and what happens to the character's body meanwhile.
quotes: BASE ASCENT TIME: (Warping Score + Warping Points gained) in days
A character with True Faith subtracts his Faith Score from the total (although the minimum remains 1 day).

entries.title: Divine Gloom
entries.summary: The Gloom form trades mundane knowledge for holy understanding: Warping Points convert into experience in holy Abilities while an equal amount is lost from mundane Abilities, and the character attracts Invisible World beings.
quotes: The character must lose the same number of Experience Points that he gained from Warping from Abilities with a mundane focus

entries.title: Divine Form
entries.summary: The Form variant makes the character a commanding, near-angelic presence with Magic Resistance and Penetration from Warping Score and Faith, but sinful acts bring extra botch dice and wounds.
quotes: The character's Penetration is equal to his Warping Score, and gains an additional bonus equal to his Faith Score multiplied by 5.
a number of additional botch dice equal to the character's Warping Score multiplied by three

entries.title: Divine Unity
entries.summary: The Unity variant makes the character personify one virtue, boosting a matching Personality Trait by Warping Score and exerting Holy Influence on those nearby and on the aura's Temper.
quotes: The Warped character adds his Warping Score to a Personality Trait determined by the virtue he is personifying

entries.title: The Virtues (for Divine Unity)
entries.summary: Reference list of Christian moral and theological virtues a Divine Unity character may personify.

entries.title: Islamic Virtues (for Divine Unity)
entries.summary: Additional Islamic virtues suitable for a character experiencing Divine Unity.

entries.title: Infernal Warping
entries.summary: Describes how Warping dominated by sin or Infernal contact produces sin-encouraging Flaws and Infernal Virtues at successive Warping Scores.
quotes: The character acquires a Minor Personality Flaw that reflects his obsession with sinful behavior.

entries.title: Causes of Infernal Warping
entries.summary: Lists the ways a character gains Infernal Warping Points: ritualised sin, Infernal auras and regiones, Infernal Powers, and botches with unholy abilities.
quotes: every time a character ritualizes a sin to acquire Confidence Points, she gains a Warping Point
if the level of the Power is 30 or more, or if a demon spends 6 or more points of Might activating the power
One Warping Point is gained for each zero on a botch dice when using an unholy Power or Infernal Supernatural Ability.

gated.title: True Faith and miracles
gated.intro: True Faith, holy influence and miracles.

entries.title: Miracles
entries.summary: How often and in what forms miracles occur in Mythic Europe (healing, punishment, miscellaneous), what makes one more likely, and how a storyguide can tune their frequency to set how Mythic the setting is.
quotes: a miracle is more likely to be granted if it is sincerely requested by a pious person, if the cause of the affliction was entirely innocent, and if an appropriate saint adds his prayers
The frequency described in the main text is a default level

entries.title: Faith Points
entries.summary: Faith Points are spent like Confidence Points for a bonus to a roll, normally one per roll; they do not regenerate on their own unless the character has True Faith.
quotes: Faith Points may be spent like Confidence Points to gain a +3 bonus to a roll, and usually a character may only spend 1 Faith Point on each roll.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine pp.56-60 Faith Points

entries.title: True Faith
entries.summary: True Faith is measured by a Score and Faith Points that work like Confidence, and the Score gives Magic Resistance; Faith Points are regained each dawn up to the Score.
quotes: TRUE FAITH MAGIC RESISTANCE: True Faith Score X 10
Each dawn, you regain a number of Faith Points up to your True Faith Score

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine Revised Edition, p.56

alsoIn.title: Taking the True Faith Virtue (Faith Score and Points)

versions.title: True Faith (overview)
versions.summary: Explains what True Faith is, who can hold it, and that it is represented by a Major Virtue, a True Faith Score and Faith Points. A character with it can pray for miracles and gains magical resistance, and on death is invested with Divine Might.
quotes: invested with Divine Might (equal to his True Faith Score multiplied by 10)
Only living people may have True Faith.

entries.title: Miracles
entries.summary: Miracles are direct divine intervention and cannot fail or be resisted.
quotes: As such, they can do anything, cannot fail, and cannot be resisted by any other power.

versions.title: Miracles (overview)
versions.summary: Introduces the optional miracle rules: miracles come directly from God, cannot be overcome by magic or other powers, and differ from saints' miracles and from learned holy powers.
quotes: The following mechanics for miracles are optional.

entries.title: Indulgences
entries.summary: Explains what an indulgence is (a reduction of a priest-decreed penance, not a payment for absolution), how its price scales with the buyer's means and the length of remission, and what a character must do afterwards to gain Reputation experience and a temporary Faith Point.
quotes: The poor donate what they feel they can afford, in most cases six Mythic pennies per season, and the wealthy at least a pound per season.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.58 Faith Points

entries.title: Vigils & Fasting
entries.summary: Rules for spending a night in prayer (a Confidence Point at the cost of a Fatigue level) and for fasting for a season (a Petitioning bonus at the cost of constant Fatigue).
quotes: A Fatigue level is lost, and will not be recovered until the character has made up a full night's sleep, but the character gains one Confidence Point that may be spent the next day on a specified virtuous task.
A fast lasts for a season and grants a +1 noncumulative bonus to Petitioning a Saint

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.87 Petitioning a Saint

entries.title: Patron Saints
entries.summary: Explains who counts as a character's patron saint for invocation, and that anyone may invoke Mary or a saint whose traditional interest fits the matter at hand, with no Piety required.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.87 Patron saints

entries.title: Example of Creating a Devout Character
entries.requires: Christian character with a positive Personality Trait: Pious
entries.summary: A worked example of assigning starting Devotion Points to saints for a pious lay character, including the extra Devotion Points a relic can grant.

entries.title: Devotion
entries.requires: Christian character with a positive Personality Trait: Pious (or the Pious Personality Flaw)
entries.summary: Introduces Devotions to particular saints as a Divine-aligned Ability-like statistic bought with separate Devotion Points rather than ordinary experience, and gives the character-generation rule for how many Devotions and Devotion Points a pious Christian starts with.
quotes: Devotions advance as an Ability, but do not use normal, generalized Experience Points, instead relying on a dedicated form of experience points called Devotion Points.
may spend Devotion Points equal to the positive score in that trait to establish Devotions

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.87 Invoking a saint

versions.title: Devotion (True Faith 2)
versions.summary: At the stated Score the character gains Premonitions and can dispel any supernatural illusion or Faerie glamour by spending a Faith Point.
quotes: the character may dispel any supernatural (magical and Infernal) illusion or Faerie glamour, no matter its level, by spending a Faith Point

entries.title: The Benefits of Devotion
entries.summary: A Devoted character can invoke any saint he has Devotion in; the Devotion score is added to the invocation roll. Also explains sacramentals as ordinary invocations of an appropriate saint, which avoid the unknown-saint penalty.
quotes: Communication + Charm + modifiers + a simple die vs. 15 + a simple die
the –15 penalty for invoking an unknown saint is not applied

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.87 Invoking a saint

entries.title: Relics & Devotion
entries.requires: Possession of a relic of a saint
entries.summary: A carried or tended relic of a saint adds to the Devotion Total when asking that saint to intercede, once a day, and also removes the unfamiliar-saint penalty.
quotes: Relic Bonus: (Faith Points in relic) x 2 bonus to Devotion Total

entries.title: The Costs of Devotion
entries.summary: A Devoted character must observe the saint's feast day each year, losing the day for seasonal activities, and loses Devotion Points if he fails to do so.
quotes: A character failing to celebrate the festival of his saint in some manner will lose at least three Devotion Points

entries.title: Gaining Devotion Points
entries.summary: Lists the activities that earn Devotion Points in play (seasons of prayer, endowing churches, guild membership, shrine visits, sponsoring art, studying hagiographies, advancing the saint's cultus, witnessing miracles, processions, pilgrimage, visions) and the usual award for each.
quotes: Spending a season engaged in prayer and meditation at a shrine to a saint earns 5 Devotion Points.
grants a number of Devotion Points equal to the Aesthetic Quality of the final artwork
worth Devotion Points equal to Quality/2

related.text: The Church Ch.3 Petitioning the Church

entries.title: False Devotion
entries.summary: Devotion can be directed at an unrecognised saint or even a mistaken entity of another realm without heresy, because dulia is not worship; true worship (latria) of anything but God is a serious sin.

entries.title: Becoming a Saint
entries.requires: Troupe decision; character died with the Personality Trait Pious at the required level
entries.summary: Sets out the conditions under which a deceased character may become a genuine saint and, separately, be formally canonised by the Church, and points to the saint-design rules in Realms of Power: The Divine.
quotes: died with a Personality Trait Pious of 6 or higher

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.60-61 Miracles
Realms of Power: The Divine p.89 Designing saints

entries.title: Ceremony (group prayer)
entries.summary: Lets a group pray together to boost a focus character's holy effect, with a group modifier based on participants' Ceremony scores, with or without a leader.
quotes: GROUP MODIFIER: total Ceremony scores – number of participants

entries.title: Invocation (Holy Method)
entries.summary: The Holy Method of calling on God's power with spoken or written prayer, costing Confidence or Faith and optionally using a stress die.
quotes: This adds Communication to your roll, and requires that you spend a point of Confidence (or Faith) to bring the effect into being.

entries.title: Meditation (Holy Method)
entries.summary: The Holy Method of achieving ecstasy through chanting or performance, with periodic Stamina rolls and a defence against Divine Ascent.
quotes: you must make a Stamina roll every ten minutes against an Ease Factor of 6
You may subtract your score in Meditation from your roll to avoid Divine Ascent

entries.title: Purity (Holy Method)
entries.summary: The Holy Method of working miracles through strenuous effort, and the rule for extending any holy ritual over hours, days or weeks to spend more Confidence or Faith.
quotes: You must engage in an activity that is strenuous enough to cause you to lose a long-term Fatigue level or suffer a Light Wound, and you use your Stamina for your effect roll.

entries.title: Holy Influence
entries.summary: How holy characters with spiritual authority inspire temporary Personality Traits in followers, by personal influence over a season or by a short ceremony, with a roll that sets the strength of the trait.
quotes: HOLY INFLUENCE: simple die + Presence + Leadership

entries.title: Personality Flaws (treating as traits)
entries.summary: States how Personality Flaws are treated as traits when rules involve Personality Traits, so holy influence can oppose them.
quotes: treat a Minor Personality Flaw as a +3 trait, and a Major Personality Flaw as a +6 trait

entries.title: Tempers
entries.summary: Rules for holy characters invoking a temper in a Dominion aura, giving bonuses or penalties to compatible or opposed actions, with descriptions of the seven tempers.
quotes: TEMPERING AN AURA: stress die + Presence + Leadership

entries.title: Personality Traits (tempers, virtues and vices)
entries.summary: A table linking each temper to related positive Personality Traits, the vice it opposes and the negative traits, with advice on noting a trait's temper.

entries.title: Schism
entries.summary: Explains how rival holy leaders invoking different tempers in the same aura can cancel each other out, which is called schism.

entries.title: Invoking God's Aid
entries.summary: Any character who can spend Confidence or a Faith Point may pray for divine help in an endeavor, with a roll and botch rule for presumption.
quotes: INVOKING GOD'S AID: stress die + Communication + Dominion Lore

entries.title: Divine Aid Bonus Table
entries.summary: Converts the invocation total into a bonus to rolls in the scene, and describes how long it lasts and how group invocations work.
quotes: the bonus will cease to operate as soon as the player fails a roll or at the end of the scene

entries.title: Invoking God's Aid in Warfare
entries.summary: Limits on invoking God's aid in military conflict and how it combines with a Trained Group's combat bonus.
quotes: only the highest Divine Aid Bonus applies to the group's combat bonus

entries.title: The Commanding Aura
entries.summary: Divinely appointed rulers and religious leaders gain Magic Resistance, a Soak bonus and an authority aura, with scores by rank and faith, and how relics and sanctions interact.
quotes: They receive a Magic Resistance score with the value listed below and a bonus to their Soak equal to their Magic Resistance score divided by 5.
In the Latin Christian world, the supreme religious leader is the Pope, with a Magic Resistance of 25.

entries.title: Player Characters and the Commanding Aura
entries.requires: Rank in an ecclesiastical or secular hierarchy
entries.summary: Rules for player characters conferring a commanding aura on others through an investiture ceremony.

entries.title: Miraculous Effects
entries.summary: The core system for holy characters: combine a Method with a Power to design an effect, roll against its level, and risk a tragedy of hubris on failure.
quotes: EFFECT TOTAL: simple die + (Characteristic) + (Method) + (Power) + Aura Bonus
They may substitute their (Faith score x 10) for their effect total when determining if they would suffer a tragedy of hubris.

entries.title: Tragedies of Hubris
entries.summary: Table of minor, major and ultimate tragedies that can befall a holy character who fails an effect roll, by how far the total fell short.
quotes: MINOR TRAGEDY (–1 TO –10)
MAJOR TRAGEDY (–11 TO –20)
ULTIMATE TRAGEDY (–21 OR MORE)

entries.title: Methods and Traditions
entries.summary: Describes the three Holy Methods, Invocation, Meditation and Purity, and the Characteristic each typically relies on.

entries.title: Learning Methods and Powers
entries.requires: True Faith or an appropriate Virtue
entries.summary: Explains how holy Methods and Powers are learned as Supernatural Abilities within a tradition, with favored Abilities that avoid the usual study penalty.
quotes: they do not have to subtract the total of their Supernatural Ability scores from their Advancement Total

entries.title: Creating New Traditions
entries.summary: Guidance for designing a new holy tradition, including how to add Methods or Powers and a limit on favored Abilities.
quotes: you should assign your new tradition a maximum of four favored Abilities

entries.title: Powers and Effects
entries.summary: How a Power's effects are designed: compute range, duration and target like Hermetic magic, replace Arcane Connections with holy connections, and add levels instead of rituals.
quotes: Instead, the Level is increased by 20.
holy effects generally add four magnitudes for a Boundary target, Year duration, or permanent duration

entries.title: Effect Combinations by Method
entries.summary: Lists which holy Powers can be activated by each of the three Methods.

entries.title: Effect Combinations by Power
entries.summary: Lists which holy Methods can activate each of the seven Powers.

entries.title: Creating New Powers and Effects
entries.summary: Advice for designing new holy effects from Hermetic guidelines or inventing a new Power.

entries.title: Adjuration (Holy Power)
entries.summary: The Power of summoning, controlling and banishing supernatural creatures, and how Invocation and Purity apply to it.

entries.title: Adjuration Guidelines
entries.summary: Effect-level guidelines for Adjuration effects such as dispelling, warding, binding and compelling supernatural creatures.
quotes: Dispel magic, infernal, or faerie effects of level less than (this effect level + 10).

entries.title: Blessing (Holy Power)
entries.summary: The Power of protecting and aiding a target by dedicating it to God, and how Invocation and Meditation apply to it.

entries.title: Blessing Guidelines
entries.summary: Effect-level guidelines for Blessing effects such as Magic Resistance, bonuses to virtuous tasks, recovery and aging bonuses.
quotes: Give a person, object, or area Magic Resistance equal to (the level of the effect + 15), which is not cumulative with other forms of resistance.

entries.title: Cursing (Holy Power)
entries.summary: The Power of bringing ruin on God's enemies, and how Invocation and Purity differ in the curses they produce.

entries.title: Cursing Guidelines
entries.summary: Effect-level guidelines for Cursing effects such as reducing Might, imposing penalties, wounding, disease and instant death.
quotes: Reduce a supernatural creature's Might by (the level of the effect + 10), assuming you overcome its resistance.

entries.title: Intervention (Holy Power)
entries.summary: The Power of making God's will visible in the physical world through signs, transformations and healing, and how Meditation and Purity apply to it.

entries.title: Intervention Guidelines
entries.summary: Effect-level guidelines for Intervention effects such as perceiving supernatural effects, transforming or mending things, healing wounds, creating regiones and raising the dead.
quotes: Create a terrestrial regio at level 1. Adding five levels increases the level by one, or adds an extra layer.

entries.title: Transcendence (Holy Power)
entries.summary: The Power of overcoming the limits of body and mind, including spiritual travel, and how Meditation and Purity apply to it.

entries.title: Transcendence Guidelines
entries.summary: Effect-level guidelines for Transcendence effects such as protection from spells, extra Soak, ignoring penalties and postponing or resolving aging crises.
quotes: You cannot be targeted by spells or powers less than (the level of this effect + 5).
increasing Soak by (the magnitude of the effect + 3)

entries.title: Understanding (Holy Power)
entries.summary: The Power of receiving holy visions and hidden knowledge, including the risk of confusion on repeated questions.

entries.title: Understanding Guidelines
entries.summary: Effect-level guidelines for Understanding effects such as visions, advice, enhanced memory and prophecy.
quotes: Reduce the number of botch dice you must roll by the magnitude of this effect

entries.title: Wonders (Holy Power)
entries.summary: The Power of conjuring items, creatures and forces of nature through Invocation, and what happens on a tragedy of hubris.

entries.title: Wonders Guidelines
entries.summary: Effect-level guidelines for Wonders effects such as creating plants, forces of nature, food, objects and animals.
quotes: Create a dangerous substance, like fire or poison, that does +(base level of the spell) damage upon contact.

entries.title: Gaining Faith Points
entries.summary: Any character can acquire Faith Points through devout acts such as pilgrimage, sacraments, tests of faith or particularly pious activities.

entries.title: Who Can Have True Faith?
entries.summary: Sidebar ruling on who is eligible for True Faith: infernalists, devotees of pagan gods, Criamon followers of the Enigma and animals cannot have it, though some monotheistic pagan philosophers might.
quotes: Since infernalists and those aligned with the Infernal Realm are in a deep state of sin, they may not have True Faith.

entries.title: Increased Faith (higher True Faith Scores)
entries.summary: Sidebar on creating characters with a True Faith Score above the basic one; each extra point of Score costs a further Major Virtue and such characters should be Mythic Companions.
quotes: Each additional increase to the character's True Faith Score above that granted by the True Faith Virtue is considered a Major Virtue.

entries.title: Gaining True Faith During Play
entries.summary: True Faith cannot be taught, learned or gained by initiation; it may be gained in play through a quest or the climax of a major story, never with a guaranteed outcome.
quotes: True Faith does not have a corresponding ability, it may not be taught or learned

entries.title: Playing a Character With True Faith
entries.summary: Describes how True Faith protects the character: it cannot be targeted, detected, suppressed or altered by magic or supernatural powers, has no ceiling on its Score, and does not require being a Mythic Companion.
quotes: True Faith may not be targeted by magic or by the powers of supernatural creatures, and may not be detected, suppressed, or altered through Intellego, Perdo, or Rego spells.

entries.title: Tests of Faith and Crises of Faith
entries.summary: God tests those with True Faith through trials; during a test the character may not spend Faith Points or use Holy Virtues. Sidebars advise on using tests as story hooks, and the text describes the crisis of faith when True Faith is lost.
quotes: In game terms, the character may no longer spend Faith Points or use Holy Virtues for the duration of the test.

entries.title: Crisis of Faith (story uses)
entries.summary: During a crisis of faith the character loses Faith Points and holy powers fail, with no set duration or recovery task; used as a story device to regain or lose True Faith.
quotes: During a crisis of faith, the character loses his Faith Points, prayers remain unanswered, and none of his holy powers work.

entries.title: True Faith and Personality
entries.summary: Spending Faith Points like Confidence is how purification shows in game terms, and saintly characters should have complementary Personality Traits; gaining a sinful trait may trigger a crisis of faith.
quotes: gaining a sinful Personality Trait may result in a crisis of faith

entries.title: Saintly Reputation
entries.summary: Miracles raise a saintly character's Reputation quickly, and a character with a True Faith Score cannot gain a negative Reputation.
quotes: Each miracle he successfully prays for counts as one noteworthy action per Faith Point he possesses, so long as there was a witness.

entries.title: Praying for Miracles
entries.summary: To pray for a miracle, a character with a Faith Point picks an effect, spends the point and rolls against the power's level; Faith Points can boost the roll, groups may pray together, and miracles have infinite Penetration.
quotes: PRAYING FOR A MIRACLE: True Faith Score + Concentration + Aura + Stress Die
Faith Points may be spent to increase this roll, adding +3 for each point spent
Miracles have an infinite Penetration: a successful miracle transcends all other powers.

entries.title: Miraculous Special Effects
entries.summary: Miracles are usually slow and subtle; asking for faster or more trivial results raises the miracle's level by a modifier.
quotes: Add the modifier to the miracle's level.

entries.title: Miracle Timeliness modifiers
entries.summary: Table of level modifiers for how quickly a miracle manifests after the prayer, from immediate to a generation.
quotes: Immediate (instantly to a few hours): +10
Generation (not longer than fifteen years): –20

entries.title: Miracle Need modifiers
entries.summary: Level modifiers reflecting how desperate, deserving or righteous the prayer is, from calamitous need to impious requests.
quotes: Calamitous (supplicant or the subjects of the prayer are in desperate personal need, such assault from supernatural forces): –15
Impious (supplicant is a pagan, infidel, or unbeliever, or the request is motivated by sin, such as pride or greed): +20

entries.title: Botching a Prayer
entries.summary: A botched prayer costs the character their Faith Points for a time, or blocks all prayers and saint invocations if they had none; it may also provoke a tragedy of hubris.
quotes: Botching a prayer roll results in the temporary loss of all Faith Points for a number of weeks equal to botches scored.

entries.title: Storyguiding Miracles
entries.summary: Advice that miracles are negotiated between player and storyguide before the roll, with the storyguide having final say, to avoid overshadowing magi; failed rolls may bring lesser aid.
quotes: God's hand cannot be forced, even by a lucky roll.

entries.title: Embodying the Light
entries.summary: Introduces the cumulative holy-light powers (Devotion, Hope, Charity) a character gains as their True Faith Score rises.
quotes: These powers are cumulative and are gained when the character gains the appropriate True Faith score.

entries.title: Hope (True Faith 3)
entries.summary: At the stated Score Faith Points spent like Confidence add more, and Magic Resistance against Mentem spells and similar powers is doubled.
quotes: adds 6 instead of 3 when spending Faith Points like Confidence
His Magic Resistance against Mentem spells (and similar supernatural powers) is doubled.

entries.title: Charity (True Faith 5)
entries.summary: At the stated Score the character radiates a Divine Empyreal aura of Voice range whose rating depends on the True Faith Score.
quotes: radiates a tangible Divine Empyreal aura (see Heaven and Earth, Divine Auras) with a rating equal to his True Faith Score minus 4
